Recall that for sound of speed $v$, the stationary observer measures $v = f_{obs}\lambda_{obs}$, so shorter $\lambda_{obs}$ means higher $f_{obs}$.
Decide which way the source at Z must be moving to crowd the wavefronts ahead of it, then compare $\lambda_{obs}$ at X and at Y with the emitted wavelength.
walkthrough: Identify the diagram feature: the wavefronts are very close together on the left around X and widely spaced on the right around Y.
State the rule: a moving source crowds wavefronts ahead of its motion and stretches them behind, changing the observed wavelength $\lambda_{obs}$.
Infer motion: crowding is on the left, so the source at Z is moving leftwards, towards X and away from Y.
Apply $v = f_{obs}\lambda_{obs}$ with constant wave speed $v$: at X, $\lambda_{obs}$ is smaller so $f_{obs} = v/\lambda_{obs}$ is greater than $F$.
At Y, $\lambda_{obs}$ is larger so $f_{obs} = v/\lambda_{obs}$ is less than $F$.
Frequency heard at X is $>F$ and frequency heard at Y is $<F$. This is option C.
